context:
Goal: every ready PR merges fast, with its lint and review still true for the head that merges.
Problem (rule): your two picks pull apart, and a bring-in on a ready PR costs a new head and a new run, so it needs your word on which pick wins.
Based on (ruling): own-923-c-ready-lanes-bring-main-in (owner, 2026-11-16 13:46 CST, ready lanes bring main in after each merge): ready and near-ready lanes bring main in after each merge. It clashes with merge-needs-current-base / own-merge-on-lint-pass (you, 18:21 CST Nov 15, "B for sure"): a head needs only a clean merge with main's tip and need not hold it.
Based on (read): runner 10 reported at 13:46 CST that a bring-in on a ready PR makes a new head and a new ready run and may send it back to draft; it happened once today (coordinator relay, not read by triage).
Departs from: main — a head needs only a clean merge with main's tip, and the CI step names only conflicting PRs; a, b and c change when a lane brings main in, and d moves the one main-in from the lane to the merge tool at merge time (decision merge-needs-current-base, your "B for sure" of 15 Nov 18:21 CST, and your 923 c pick, after each merge, ready lanes).
Meanwhile: the coordinator holds the agent that would write this rule until you pick; ready PRs behind main but clean still merge as they are.
Based on (read): the consultant's view (coordinator relay 13:26 CST): a lane brings main in only on conflict or when about to merge with its tree not proven; never on a timer. The coordinator's web read (sonnet Explore, partly unverified): with a gate before main moves, syncing only on conflict wins; syncing after every merge is the "require up to date" treadmill, about 34 min per run (bors-ng).

lastAnswer.note: d) Lanes bring main in only on conflict; the merge tool does one main-in at merge time and keeps the green run (needs #3481 and #3552 on main). Saved on the page 14:20 CST Nov 17.

options.gain: Few new heads, so ready PRs rarely go back to draft or wait for a new run.
options.how: A lane brings main in once, just before its last lint, so lint and review sit on a head that has main. After that it brings main in only on a conflict. A ready PR that is behind but clean merges as it is.
options.label: A lane brings main in once, right before its lint; later only if it conflicts
options.lose: A ready PR can merge several merges behind main, so main's own run after the merge may catch a clash the PR run did not.

options.gain: Every PR tests against the newest main before it merges.
options.how: After every merge to main, each ready or lint-passed PR brings main in.
options.label: After each merge, ready and lint-passed PRs bring main in (as you typed)
options.lose: Each bring-in makes a new head and a new run, and may send a ready PR back to draft, so the queue slows while lanes keep re-running.

options.gain: The fewest new heads; ready PRs stay ready.
options.how: A PR brings main in only when it conflicts with main's tip; nothing else is touched.
options.label: Only a PR that conflicts brings main in
options.lose: Lint and review may sit on a head that is far behind main, so a clean-looking PR can still break main.

options.gain: Fewest runs and no hand main-ins; matches the merge-queue practice of GitHub, Mergify and Zuul, where the queue, not the author, updates the base (coordinator's web read, partly unverified).
options.how: A lane brings main in only when it conflicts, or when it is about to merge with its tree not proven; never on a timer. The merge tool does one main-in at merge time and keeps the green run: #3481 carries lane lint across a clean main merge, #3552 merges main into a lagging head at lint time (consultant's order: #3481, #3552, #3383).
options.label: Lanes bring main in only on conflict; the merge tool does one main-in at merge time and keeps the green run (needs #3481 and #3552 on main)
options.lose: Relies on two unmerged PRs; until they land, a lane still merges main by hand at merge time.

title: When should a lane bring main into its branch: once before lint, after every merge, or only on a conflict?
why: It gives the fewest runs and no hand main-ins, and it is how merge queues work; the cost is that it needs #3481 and #3552 on main first. Recommended by the coordinator and consultant, not owner-typed.
